text:
Alex: Heads up — starting a canary for model v3-quant (10% traffic) across us-west/us-east/eu-central. Quick design question: for automatic fallbacks during the rollout, should we prefer model-variant fallback (v3-quant -> v3-small) or regional failover first if a region is overloaded?
Maya: My vote is model-variant in-region first. Cross-region adds latency and egress costs. But we need capacity-aware ordering: if GPU pool exhausted, fallback to smaller/quantized variant; if still failing, then region failover. :thinking:
Prashant: Agree. Propose an explicit priority chain: 1) local compatible variant (same region) 2) same-region smaller instance/tier 3) cross-region same model (if egress/quota allows) 4) degrade response (shorter max_tokens) 5) surface 429/503 to client. Telemetry must tag which step triggered.
Sophia: From UX side, we should show the active fallback chain in the Rollout details panel and surface a per-step toggle (allow cross-region: on/off). Default cross-region off for enterprise tenants. Also add a simulated 'apply fallback' button so devs can run a dry-run.
DeployBot: deploy v3-canary 10% -> us-west/us-east/eu-central. canary_id=canary-2005-01. status=started. (This is an automated note)
Samira: Telemetry requirements: emit a metric fallback.count by fallback_type (variant|tier|region|degrade) and fallback.latency_delta. Add alert if fallback.count/fallback.attempts > 0.01 for >1min. Also capture per-route and per-tenant breakdowns.
Kevin: Quota/legal: we need a guard that prevents automatic cross-region fallback if the org's egress_quota_remaining < threshold or if customer has region_restrictions. That should be evaluated before step 3 in Prashant's chain.
Alex: Also call out pinned customers (customer.pinned=true) — skip fallbacks entirely and return controlled failure or queue. We can't silently degrade pinned SLAs.
Prashant: API suggestion: add a fallback_policy array with ordered actions and selectors. Example in thread (proto):
```json
{"fallback_policy": [
  {"action": "variant_swap", "selector": "compatible_same_region", "conditions": {"gpu_pool_utilization_lt": 0.95}},
  {"action": "instance_tier_swap", "selector": "same_region_smaller_tier"},
  {"action": "cross_region_route", "selector": "same_model", "conditions": {"egress_quota_ok": true}},
  {"action": "response_degrade", "params": {"max_tokens_factor": 0.7}},
  {"action": "reject", "params": {"status": 429}}
]}
```
Prashant: The API will also return a fallback_reason in response headers when a fallback occurs so apps can log it.
OpsBot: Runbook suggestion when cross-region fallback fires: 1) notify infra on-call if >0.5% of total traffic for 2m, 2) annotate the canary and mute canary if >5% fallbacks, 3) automatically open a P0 if fallbacks coincide with increased latency >250ms.
Maya: UI note — add a tiny banner in the console that shows "Active fallback: variant_swap" with a :eyes: emoji and link to timeline traces. Also show historical fallback rate for the canary.
Kevin: Implementation detail — routing layer must evaluate the fallback policy atomically with quota checks to avoid race conditions. Also add a circuit-breaker counter per region/model to avoid thundering herd on recovery.
Alex: Edge-case: what if variant_swap returns lower-quality results that fail our quality evals? We should wire the evals system to abort canary rollouts if quality regression > tolerance. That ties into Optimize.
Samira: I'll add telemetry names and a Grafana dashboard mock: fallback.count, fallback.by_type, fallback.latency_delta, fallback.tenant_rate. Will draft alerts.
Sophia: I'll prototype the Rollout UI with a fallback chain editor (drag to reorder) and show 'simulated impact' numbers.
Prashant: I'll own the API schema + validations and add integration tests that exercise each fallback step. Plan to PR by EOW. :shipit:
Alex: Great — thanks everyone. Keeping this thread as the source of truth for policy + small UX/telemetry scope.
